channel.title: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report
channel.description: The Weekly Volcanic Activity Report is a cooperative project between the Smithsonian's Global Volcanism Program and the US Geological Survey's Volcano Hazards Program. Updated by 2300 UTC every Thursday, these notices are preliminary and subject to change as events are studied in more detail. This is not a comprehensive list of eruptions during the week, but rather a summary of activity that meet selected criteria. Carefully reviewed, detailed reports are published in the Bulletin of the Global Volcanism Network.

item.title: Asosan (Japan) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - New Unrest
item.description:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that the amplitude of volcanic tremors at Asosan began to increase at around 1900 on 12 August, fluctuated for a few days, and further intensified at 1500 on 14 August. During a field survey that same day scientists measured a high sulfur dioxide emission rate of 2,700 tons per day (t/d), notably increased from 700 t/d on 28 July and 1,200 t/d on 6 August. The Alert Level was raised to 3 (on a scale of 1-5) at 1545 and the public was warned that eruptive products may impact areas within 2 km of the crater. Continuous Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data suggested that magma was accumulating beneath Kusasenri. Webcams show no significant changes in conditions within the crater; white plumes rose as high as 900 m above the Nakadake Crater I rim during 12-17 August.

Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

item.title: Etna (Italy) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported eruptive activity at Etna?s summit craters during 10-16 August characterized by explosive activity and ash emissions at both Voragine Crater (VOR) and Northeast Crater (NEC), and effusive activity from several vents within the Valle del Bove. Explosive activity at VOR persisted during most of the week with ash emissions mainly drifting S and SE. Emissions significantly intensified during the afternoon of 13 August and Strombolian activity was visible the afternoon of 16 August. Explosive activity on 17 August generated a notable ash plume that rose around 6 km (19,700 ft) a.s.l. and drifted SE. Several intra-crater explosive episodes at NEC were recorded during the week. A brief explosion on 15 August produced an ash plume that drifted S. A series of short-lived explosions on 16 August produced ash plumes that drifted SE. Ash emissions intensified later that day. Lava effusion from multiple vents was variable through the week. During 10-12 August flows from vents at 1,900 m, 2,090 m, and 2,750 m elevations were active, though by 13 August effusion at the 2,090 m elevation vent had ceased. Early on 14 August a pit crater formed at an elevation of 3,000 m and produced intermittent gas emissions for a brief period. Strombolian activity continued and the leading lava flows from the active vents advanced during 13-16 August, reaching an elevation of 1,395 m between Rocca delle Palombe and Rocca Musarra. On 17 August a new effusive vent opened in Valle del Bove, at an elevation of 2,350 m, which triggered the collapse of the E flank of the Monte Rittmann cone along with an ash emission. The new vent produced a lava flow that traveled 500 m and rapidly cooled. By the afternoon of 17 August, the lava field fed by multiple vents was generally cooling. The vent at 1,900 m elevation remained active and continued to effuse lava with the flow front reaching an elevation of approximately 1,600 m. Overall effusion during 7-17 August covered an approximate area of 1.7 square kilometers and had estimated volumes ranging from 5.6 to 7.6 × 10? cubic meters. The volcano Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile.

Source: Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV)

item.title: Karangetang (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) and a news source reported that an eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua) continued during 12-19 August. Lava began to effuse from North Crater on 9 August, advancing about 700 m S into the saddle between the North and South (Kawah Utama or Main) craters, then advanced W for about 400 m and NNW for about 1 km, igniting vegetation fires. Lava flows continued to be active during 12-18 August and descended 1 km SW. Rumbling was often heard, which was sometimes accompanied by grayish-white puffs that rose as high as 150 m and drifted NNE. Residents in Pehe Village reported that vegetation between the Kinali and Hiung rivers had ignited and was burning. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 1.5 km away from both craters, with an extension to 2.5 km on the NW and SW flanks of North Crater.

Sources: Antara News,Antara News,Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Klyuchevskoy (Russia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that a new eruption at Klyuchevskoy began with Strombolian explosions and lava fountaining at the summit crater on 15 August. The temperature of a thermal anomaly identified in satellite images began increasing at 1541. Activity continued on 16 August and at 2236 the Aviation Color Code (ACC) was raised to Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-color scale). A series of large collapses began in the Apakhonchichsky drainage on the SE flank at 2320 and lasted about 30 minutes. Ash clouds from the collapse and possible explosions rose 7-8 km (22,960-26,250 ft) a.s.l. and drifted 50 km E, though according to the Tokyo Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) ash plumes may have risen as high as 9.1 km (30,000 ft) a.s.l. The ACC was raised to Orange at 2343. Strombolian explosions and lava fountaining continued on 17 August and collapsed hot material descended the Apakhonchichsky drainage. Ash plumes rose 6 km (19,680 ft) a.s.l. and drifted 420 km ESE. Gas-and-ash plumes rose to 5.5 km (18,100 ft) a.s.l. on 18 August and drifted 400 km ESE. Dates and times are provided in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC); specific events are indicated in local time where specified.

Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

item.title: Krakatau (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Krakatau during 13-20 August. White-and-gray plumes rose as high as 150 m above the summit on 13 August and drifted in various directions. No emissions were observed the next day. During 16-18 August white, gray, and black plumes rose as high as 400 m above the summit and drifted mainly NW, N, NE, and E. Multiple eruptive events per day were recorded during 16-17 August, and several webcam images showed incandescent material being ejected above the crater. According to a news report, residents of Tejang Village (20 km NNE) on Sebesi Island reported ashfall during 16-18 August and adverse health effects due to ash in the air. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 3 km away from summit.

Sources: Antara News,Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Sinabung (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - New Unrest
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that seismicity at Sinabung is continuing to increase. There was a notable increase in the number of deep volcanic earthquakes and signals indicating emissions during 1-12 August. Additionally, some low-frequency and hybrid earthquakes were detected. Emissions had become denser, were grayish-white, and rose as high as 1 km above the summit. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4), though at 1000 on 13 August the exclusion zone was increased to 3 km from the summit and 4.5 km on the SE flank.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Aira (Japan) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 10-17 August. Crater incandescence was visible in nighttime webcam images. The monitoring networks recorded a total of 14 eruptive events and one explosion. Eruptive events during 10-15 August generated ash plumes that rose as high as 1.8 km above the summit and drifted in multiple directions. Emissions were sometimes continuous, notably during 0020-0150 on 12 August, during 1906-2220 on 14 August, and during 1019-1150 on 15 August. An explosion at 2232 on 13 August ejected large blocks 800-1,100 m from the vent; plume characteristics were not reported. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a 5-level scale), and the public was warned to be cautious within 2 km of both the Minimadake and Showa craters.

Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

item.title: Ambae (Vanuatu) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Wellington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that daily ash-and-gas plumes at Ambae were identified in satellite and webcam images during 13-18 August rising 1.5-4.6 km (5,000-15,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting in multiple directions. Occasionally the ash emissions were intermittent, and sulfur dioxide plumes were also occasionally identified. Weather clouds sometimes obscured views. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 0-5), and the public was warned to stay outside of Danger Zone B, defined as a 3-km radius around the active vents in Lake Voui, and to stay away from drainages during heavy rains.

Source: Wellington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

item.title: Dukono (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity at Dukono continued during 13-19 August. White plumes rose as high as 400 m above the summit on 13 August. On the other days white-and-gray ash plume rose as high as 1.5 km above the summit and drifted in various directions. The Alert Level remained at Level 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 4 km away from the Malupang Warirang Crater.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Great Sitkin (United States) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater during 12-19 August based on webcam and satellite images. The flow advanced mainly E. Minor earthquakes were detected daily, likely associated with rockfalls on the growing dome. Weather clouds often obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Watch (the third level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the third color on a four-color scale).

Source: US Geological Survey Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO)

item.title: Ibu (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 13-19 August, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Gray or white-to-gray ash plumes rose 300-800 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions, especially towards the N and NE on most days; emissions were not visible on 19 August. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the active crater and 3.5 km away from the N crater wall opening.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Kanlaon (Philippines) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported continuing eruptive activity at Kanlaon during 12-18 August. The seismic network recorded 0-7 daily volcanic earthquakes; the counts included 1-3 daily periods of tremor during 14-15 and 17 August, lasting two minutes to one hour and 34 minutes. Sulfur dioxide emissions ranged from 887 to 3,304 tonnes per day. Volcanic emissions rose as high as 200 m above the summit and drifted NNE, ENE, and E. A grayish ash emission lasting 92 minutes on 13 August rose 200 m above the summit and drifted ENE. On 14 August there were five ash emissions and on 15 August there were three ash emissions, each lasting five minutes to just over an hour. One of the 14 August ash emissions, at 0549, was grayish and rose 200 m above the summit and drifted N. On 17 August one ash emission was recorded for 94 minutes. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 0-5); the public was warned to stay out of the 4-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) and pilots were advised to avoid flying close to the summit.

Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)

item.title: Kilauea (United States) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by episodic fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter from craters along the SW margin of Halema`uma`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 13-18 August. The 53rd episode of lava fountaining began at 1545 on 12 August and ended at 0123 on 13 August, after 9.6 hours of continuous activity. The average effusion rate was 135 cubic meters per second; the highest peak was 230 cubic meters per second, occurring at around 1715. An estimated 6 million cubic meters of lava erupted and covered 40-50 percent of the Halema`uma`u Crater floor. The S vent did not produce a fountain, but instead emitted flames. Large lava overflows occurred at the S vent at 1526 and 1538, each lasting approximately 5-6 minutes. A small flow occurred at the W vent (previously referred to as a new collapse feature) at 1531 and lasted for 28 minutes, ending 14 minutes after the start of the fountaining episode. Two more flows, from the S vent and the W vent, began at 1602 and 1603, respectively. The flow from the S vent only lasted three minutes. In contrast, the flow at the W vent lasted 14 minutes and intensified until it finally overflowed and drained into the S vent. Weak-to-moderate intermittent incandescence at the N vent was observed during 13-14 and 17-18 August, while the S vent appeared dark. A few weak flashes of glow occurred at the W vent during 17-18 August. During most of the week weather conditions from Hurricane Lala obscured views. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Advisory (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Yellow (the second lowest color on a four-color scale).

Source: US Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO)

item.title: Lewotobi (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity continued at Lewotobi Laki-Laki during 13-18 August. Multiple daily gray ash plumes rose 200-1,000 m above the summit and drifted NW, W, and SW. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 5 km away from the center of Laki-Laki.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Lewotolok (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported increasing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 13-19 August. White plumes rose as high as 500 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions. Incandescent material was ejected above the summit and onto the flanks daily, as far as 400 m S and 500 m SE. Ash plumes rose 500 m above the summit and drifted SW at 1317 on 15 August and rose 400 m above the summit and drifted W at 1900 that same day. Real-time Seismic Amplitude Measurements (RSAM) data showed a sharp increase on 16 August. White-and-gray plumes rose as high as 500 m on 17 August. Observers reported that during the morning of 18 August lava had flowed over the crater rim and traveled 400 m down the S flank. The flow had advanced through the day and by the evening was 1.2 km long. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4). The public was warned to stay 2 km away from the summit, but on 19 August the exclusion zone was expanded to 3 km on the S and SE flanks.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Mayon (Philippines) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported that the eruption at Mayon continued at low levels during 12-17 August. Each day the seismic network recorded 4-11 volcanic earthquakes; one rockfall was recorded each day on 15 and 18 August. An ash emission was visible on 12 August. Sulfur dioxide emissions (SO?) averaged 1,857-3,2957 tonnes per day (t/d) over this reporting period, but increased on 17 August to 8,393 t/d, well above the average of 2,532 t/d recorded since 5 August. The abrupt rise followed recent inflation of the N and E flanks recorded by electronic tilt deformation stations. Emissions declined to an average of 6,878 t/d on 18 August. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a 0-5 scale) and the public was reminded to stay away from the 6-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ). PHIVOLCS recommended that civil aviation authorities advise pilots to avoid flying close to the summit.

Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)

item.title: Merapi (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Merapi (on Java) continued during 13-20 August with lava avalanches produced by the active lava dome on the upper SW flank. The seismic network recorded as many as nine lava avalanches per day that traveled as far as 1.9 km down the Sat/Putih and Krasak, drainages on the SW flank. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 3-7 km away from the summit, based on location.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Nyamulagira (DR Congo) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The eruption at Nyamulagira continued during July and August based on satellite data. Incandescence on the floor of the summit caldera was visible in multiple partly or mostly cloudy satellite images. Active lava flows on the NNW and NW flanks, near the crater rim, were identified in a 20 July image and an active flow on the SW flank was visible in a 9 August image. The active parts of the flows were apparent in a beautifully clear 14 August image. Hot spots on the NNW flow were located as far as 700 m from the crater rim, a few hotspots on the NW flow were around 460 m from the crater rim, and the SW flow was mostly hot and about 2.8 km long.

Source: Copernicus Browser

item.title: Rincon de la Vieja (Costa Rica) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Observatorio Vulcanológico y Sismológico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA) reported that small phreatic eruptions at Rincón de la Vieja were recorded by the seismic and infrasound networks at 1516 on 13 August and at 1050 on 19 August, but not visually observed. A possible small phreatic eruption was recorded at 2220 on 13 August. The Alert Level remained at 3 (Caution) and the Aviation Color Code remained Orange.

Source: Observatorio Vulcanologico y Sismologico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA)

item.title: Sabancaya (Peru) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Geofísico del Perú?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanológico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 10-16 August. The seismic network detected 41 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the period. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 600 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km E and SE. Moderate sulfur dioxide (SO?) emissions averaged 838 tonnes per day, and seven thermal anomalies (each 1 MW or less) associated with the lava dome were identified. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the third level on a four-color scale) and the public was warned to stay outside of a 12 km radius from the summit.

Source: Instituto Geofísico del Perú (IGP)

item.title: Semeru (Indonesia) - Report for 13 August-19 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 13-19 August, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Daily white-to-gray or gray ash plumes rose 300-1,200 m above the summit and drifted multiple directions. The Alert Level remained at 3 (the second lowest level on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay at least 5 km away from the Jonggring Saloko Crater in all directions, 13 km from the summit on the SE flank along the Kobokan drainage, and 500 m from the banks of the Kobokan drainage as far as 17 km SE of the summit.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)
